en: The preceptor, appearing as the form of Vajradhara, should instantly visualize his right hand as having the form of a five-pronged vajra with its fingers joined; therein he should meditate upon a sun disk born from the syllable *ĀḤ*, empowered by the syllable *ĀḤ*. With his left hand, instantly visualized in the shape of a lotus petal with its fingers joined, he should meditate upon a moon disk born from the syllable *A*, empowered by that same syllable. Between these two, he should contemplate the central thread of the held rosary as being the very nature of Vajrasattva, while the eight threads extending toward the cardinal and intermediate directions [should be understood likewise].

Having instantly visualized the pills as having the nature of Padmapāṇi, Maitreya, Gaganagañja, Samantabhadra, Vajrapāṇi, Mañjuśrī, Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, and Kṣitigarbha, and the upper pill as having the nature of a stūpa of the qualities such as the powers (*bala*) and fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), which are the very forms of the Tathāgatas beginning with Vairocana; and having caused Vajrasattva and the others, drawn by rays from the seed-syllable in the heart, to enter [the pills] each according to their respective [deities].

Visualizing oneself for a moment as the form of the Master Vajradhara, with the fingers of the right hand appearing as five-pronged vajras, one should contemplate the sun arising from the syllable *āḥ* and being blessed by the syllable *āḥ*.

Having visualized the fingers of the left hand as lotus petals, which are instantly consecrated by a moon disc arisen from the syllable *āḥ*, one should contemplate that the central thread of the rosary held between them is the very nature of Vajrasattva.

The threads of the cardinal and intermediate directions are the nature of Padmapāṇi, Maitreya, Gaganagañja, Samantabhadra, Vajrapāṇi, Mañjuśrī, Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, and Kṣitigarbha; the beads of the rosary are the nature of the Tathāgatas, such as Vairocana and the rest.

The Sūtradhara, having for a moment intensely visualized himself as being of the nature of the Dharma-caitya—consisting of the powers, the fearlessnesses, and so forth—causes Vajrasattva and the others, who have been summoned by the light rays from the seed-syllable at his heart, to enter himself in their respective forms.

*akkharu kāraṇarūa sohia mantavisāru gaṇi a asaṃkhu alikku sihya itatta visāru |* (Translation of the Apabhraṃśa verse: The syllable, whose form is the cause, is purified; the Lord of Mantras is the aggregate, the infinite, the unstruck (*alika*), the disciple, the essence, the Victor. (Note: This is a *Catuṣpīṭha* Apabhraṃśa song.)
*Oṃ pade pade mahājñānaṃ sarvabuddham ahaṃ bhave hūṃ 3 ho 3 aḥ khaṃ svāhā.* With this mantra, one should perform the consecration.
*oṃ pade pade mahājñānaṃ sarvabuddham ahaṃ bhave hūṃ hūṃ ho ho aḥ khaṃ svāhā.* By means of this mantra, one should empower [the object].
One should consecrate with the water from the *kalaśa* and perform worship. Thus concludes the consecration of the rosary (*akṣasūtra*). || 0 ||
"Having conferred the empowerment with the water from the vase, one should offer worship"—this is the consecration of the rosary.

The abbreviated method for the consecration of the rosary (*akṣasūtra*) is as follows: having visualized the Speech-Vajra (*vāgvajra*) and unified it with the Knowledge-Being (*jñānasattva*), one should contemplate its transformation into the form of the rosary; then, having consecrated it with water from a vase and performed worship, one should recite the heart-mantra of the Speech-Vajra one hundred and eight times. This is the abbreviated consecration of the rosary.

In brief: having visualized the rosary as Vāgvajra and unified it with the Jñānasattva, one contemplates that [Jñānasattva] transforming into the form of the rosary; then, having conferred empowerment with water from a vase and made offerings, one recites the essence-mantra of Vāgvajra one hundred and eight times. This is the ritual for the consecration of the rosary according to the summary.

Now, the procedure for the rosary as taught in the Vajraḍāka Tantra is written.
Now, the ritual for the rosary as taught in the *Vajraḍāka-tantra* shall be written:
for pacification, enrichment, subjugation, malevolent rites, and indeed for all activities.
He is proclaimed as Vajradhara; he who sustains the city is highly praised.

Putrañjīva has indeed taught that for pacifying, enriching, magnetizing, subjugating, and all ritual activities, the Vajradhara has explained them as equal; thus he thoroughly demonstrated the *bodhicitta*.
Crystal, mother-of-pearl, pearl, and all kinds of minerals,
as well as conch and *vṛṣāvarta*— these increase youth and health.
Crystal, mother-of-pearl, pearls, and all those born from the elements, as well as conch shells—these increase one's lifespan and youth.
One should employ the mantra with gold, silver, and likewise lotus seeds; by this, one attains sovereign power.
With gold and likewise with silver, and similarly with the supreme lotus seed, through the mantra of this application, one will attain supreme sovereignty.
With saffron and other fragrant substances,
especially with coral, with red sandalwood, and likewise with another red substance.
With fragrant substances such as saffron, and especially with coral, red sandalwood, and likewise other red [substances],...
The practitioner, having formed a pill, should apply the king of mantras;
it is excellent for subjugation and enchantment, bestowing fruit upon the practitioner.
The practitioner should prepare the pills through the application of the King of Mantras; they will bestow supreme empowerment and passion, granting the excellent fruit to the practitioner.
Likewise, when used with a rudrākṣa or an ariṣṭa seed,
it bestows its fruit upon those reciting it during a fierce malevolent rite (abhicāra) while standing in battle— or [with] human bone— by means of this [mantra].
With *ru*, *trākṣa*, and likewise with *lung-tang*, seeds, and human bone—by reciting these, the most excellent results are bestowed for wrathful and forceful rites.
One hundred and one for pacification, likewise one hundred and eight for enrichment;
twenty-five for subjugation, and fifty for the accomplishment of mantras.
For pacifying, one hundred; for enriching, likewise eight more; for magnetizing, twenty-five; and for the accomplishment of mantras, one thousand.
One should employ sixty pills for the rite of fierce sorcery;
thus the power of the mantra is accomplished for the compassionate practitioner.
This is the application of the sixty pills for the rites of fierce sorcery; it will be accomplished through the power of mantra by the practitioner whose nature is compassion.
All the Arhats have prepared pills for the interior of the stūpa;
"the witness of the Dharma" refers to the stūpas, while "the realm of phenomena" (dharmadhātu) is the middle [stūpa].
All the pills are Arhats; above them, one should visualize a stūpa. Because the stūpa is the mountain of the Dharma, the dharmadhātu is at its center.
It brings about all accomplishments and is auspicious; one should wrap it with a golden thread [or tie it in a knot]. Alternatively, [one may use] a cotton thread spun by a young maiden.
The peaceful *Sarvasiddhikara* [mantra] should be strung with a golden thread; alternatively, it may be strung with a thread spun by a young maiden upon a cotton cloth.

Bound with a cord of human hair, or even with that of a horse, or with a cord of hair from a charnel ground mixed with the fur of a dog.
Having properly formed the pill by tying it with a thread, one should perform the cruel rite;
for whichever rite is prescribed, the corresponding thread should be used, as stated in brief.
Having formed the medicinal pellets, one should correctly perform the wrathful rites; as for which thread is used for which rite, that has also been explained in brief.
In rites of pacification, enrichment, subjugation, and even in rites of sorcery,
the wise practitioner should employ [the mudrās] mounted on the index finger and so forth in their proper sequence.

For the rites of pacification, enrichment, magnetizing, and wrathful activity as well, the wise one, having placed [the fingers] in equipoise upon the toes and so forth, should perform them according to the proper sequence.

Likewise, having performed the recitation while focused in meditative absorption upon that which is mounted on the thumb by virtue of its nature as a universal attractor, it is accomplished; there is no doubt in this matter.
Likewise, having joined the thumbs together and remained in meditative equipoise with the nature of summoning all, one will achieve accomplishment; of this there is no doubt.
Thus ends the rule for the rosaries of various ritual acts.
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the rosary of various activities.
